trust_decision.summary: Each scaffolder SCM action decides, inside its own handler or its per-package helper, whether the outbound SCM request may be authenticated with the app/integration credential (integration token, GitHub App installation token, Azure PAT) or must use a token supplied as action input; the decision is a fresh independent read of scaffolder.requireScmUserCredentials at every construction site, defaulting to off (fail-open).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unintended GitHub authentication fallback'; the only place GitHub silently swaps the user token for provider credentials is getOctokitOptions' githubCredentialsProvider.getCredentials call, so an engineer reading only the summary lands here.

fix_sites.entry_point: publish:github:pull-request (own clientFactory, does not go through getOctokitOptions)

github module wiring: github:actions:dispatch, github:autolinks:create, github:deployKey:create, github:environment:create, github:issues:label, github:issues:create, github:repo:create, github:repo:push, github:webhook, publish:github, publish:github:pull-request, github:pages:enable, github:branch-protection:create
getClient (gitlab:group:ensureExists, gitlab:group:access, gitlab:issues:create, gitlab:issue:edit, gitlab:projectDeployToken:create, gitlab:projectVariable:create, gitlab:pipeline:trigger)
assertScmUserCredentials (shared by the four fetch actions)
scaffolder core plugin wiring of the four fetch actions

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fetchContents/fetchFile are the public lower-level read helpers in @backstage/plugin-scaffolder-node, documented as 'can be used in your own actions'; the setting's own docs say custom actions and readers that do not take a user-token input are not affected, so a solver can argue the enforcement belongs only in the action wrappers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: fetch:plain / fetch:template with a relative local path (e.g. './skeleton') or any non-SCM URL must keep working with no token; the sink is the same fetchContents call, so an over-broad 'no token = reject' at the top of the handler breaks the most common local-template case (and bitbucketServer/Azure reads, which have no user-token input at all).

O6_input_shapes: token present but empty/falsy string - treated as omitted by the `!ctx.input.token` checks
token supplied by the user - action proceeds, and the integration credentials provider must not be called at all
fetch url as an absolute URL vs a relative path resolved against ctx.templateInfo.baseUrl
GitLab setUserAsOwner / ownerUsername combined with a user token - must be rejected
bitbucketServer token defaulting written as `token ?? integration.token` (and the option's fail-open ordering) vs bitbucketCloud's ternary on the auth header

O8_uncovered_routes.route: gitlab:user:info reads the authenticated GitLab user via getClient, which falls back to integrationConfig.config.token when the optional `token` input is absent; the module never passes the new flag
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a read-only informational action, and the advisory/changeset calls out mutation actions (plus the four fetch actions) as the supported surface - reads that merely report identity were never covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling file to the publish:gitlab fix site; registered at plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-gitlab/src/module.ts:66

O8_uncovered_routes.route: fetch:cookiecutter calls the same fetchContents helper with no token and no check, so a template can still have the app credential read a private GitHub/GitLab repo
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: cookiecutter is a legacy optional module and the setting's docs enumerate only fetch:plain, fetch:plain:file, fetch:template and fetch:template:file as the covered reads.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package, three packages away from the GitHub landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a further gitlab:* action that builds its client with getClient and forgets the new option
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getClient already defaults to the integration token and the option defaults to false, so a copied action silently fails open; this exact sibling already exists at the pinned commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an action that builds its client through an injectable clientFactory instead of getOctokitOptions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix needed a second, inline check here precisely because this wrapper does not reach the shared helper - a maintainer adding another overridable factory would repeat the pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a non-action SCM caller (autocomplete provider) using the same client helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: autocomplete is registered from the same module init with only `integrations`, so it is the natural place for another credential-bearing call path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a further read helper or a custom action calling fetchContents/fetchFile directly
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is a published helper ('can be used in your own actions') that already accepts a token, so guarding it is the obvious shared place a maintainer might pick next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a sibling SCM module adopting scaffolder.requireScmUserCredentials
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: each SCM module re-reads the config independently in its own module.ts, so a new provider either copies the option (and its own fail-open default) or forgets it entirely.

O9_family: confused deputy / broken authorization on credential selection (CWE-441, CWE-863)

O10_build.toolchain: yarn 4 workspaces, @backstage/cli (jest, tsc, eslint); packages under plugins/ and packages/
O10_build.project_tests: per-package jest unit tests that mock SCM HTTP with msw/nock, e.g. plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-azure/src/actions/azure.test.ts, plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-bitbucket-cloud/src/actions/bitbucketCloudPipelinesRun.test.ts, plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-github/src/util.test.ts, plugins/scaffolder-backend/src/scaffolder/actions/builtin/fetch/plain.test.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (!token) throw` unconditionally inside the two shared helpers (getOctokitOptions and getClient), treating the report's GitHub example as the whole list - this breaks the flag-off path and still leaves bitbucket-cloud, bitbucket-server, azure, the four fetch actions and gitlab:user:info untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The platform UrlReader implementations and DefaultGithubCredentialsProvider in @backstage/integration also fall back to integration/app credentials, but they sit below the scaffolder setting this advisory introduces.
